newsitem.title: RUSSIA: IMF revises up Russia budget deficit target ratio.
newsitem.headline: IMF revises up Russia budget deficit target ratio.

text.p: The International Monetary Fund has revised up Russia's target 1996 budget deficit ratio due to higher-than-expected yields on domestic debt before the presidential election, a finance ministry official said.

Jochen Wermuth, head of the finance ministry's economic expert group, said the 1996 target had been revised to 5.25 percent of gross domestic product, from four percent to take account of higher borrowing costs.
He said the new target represented a loosening in terms of overall spending, but meant that Russia would have to tighten policy in the second half.
The IMF, which uses different methods from Russia for calculating the budget deficit, had expected Russia to spend 30 trillion roubles in 1996 servicing its GKO Treasury Bills.
But Wermuth said actual debt servicing was 90 trillion roubles, pushed up by yields which peaked at over 200 percent, the highest real interest rates in the world.

The first-half deficit, using IMF methods, was 77.3 trillion roubles, or 6.3 percent of gross domestic product (GDP). GDP is also calculated differently by the IMF and by Russia's State Statistics Committee, he said.

The Russian figures put the first-half federal deficit, using the definition in Russia's budget law, at four percent of GDP. The total deficit, including local authority spending, off-budget and other consolidated data, was six percent of GDP.
The 1996 budget targets a federal deficit of 3.8 percent of GDP for the whole year.
The IMF, which is backing Russia's economic reform programme with a three-year $10 billion loan, delayed handing over the July tranche of the loan because of concern about low Russian tax collection.

The money for July was handed over this month, although Wermuth admitted this had only been possible because of the revision to the IMF target. Economists said the Fund was likely to pay out the tranche for August as Russia was broadly fulfilling the terms of the agreement.
